When a duplicate charge shows up, check the order's idempotency keys via `tidectl orders show <id>`: if it's the same key twice, the second line is just an authorization that self-expires in 7 days; if the keys differ, it's a real second charge, so verify via `payment_events`/webhook log and refund the extra charge from the Paylane dashboard (opening a bug if the cause is on our side).

Sources: .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

When a buyer sees two identical transactions, look up the order (`tidectl orders show <id>`) — if both charges share the same idempotency key, the second is just an authorization that auto-expires in 7 days and no action is needed; if the keys differ, it's a real duplicate charge, so check `payment_events`/webhook log, refund the extra charge via the Paylane dashboard, note it on the order, and file a bug if it's caused by our system.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

Each admission gets a single-use QR token that Gatekeeper sends to tide-api, which consumes it atomically (`UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`); a second scan at any gate is rejected with "already used" plus the time/gate of the first entry (this fixed BUG-017, where two gates accepted the same admission within two seconds).

Sources: .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/memory/decisions.md (ADR-011), .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md, .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/docs/bugs.md (BUG-017), .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/memory/architecture.md

Each ticket's QR token is consumed atomically on first scan (`UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`), so a race between two gates can only let one succeed; any later attempt gets "already used" with the time/gate of the first entry, and Gatekeeper's offline mode keeps a local list to reconcile conflicts afterward.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md (ADR-011), tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md

TLS certificates renew automatically via a certbot systemd timer (DNS challenge, every 12h) that runs a deploy hook to rebuild the HAProxy bundle and reload without dropping connections; if that automation fails (alert fires within 14 days of expiry), the manual fallback is: `certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal` on `kelp-1`, verify with `openssl x509 -enddate`, rebuild via `haproxy-cert-bundle`, `systemctl reload haproxy`, then check externally with `curl -vI`.

Sources: .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, .gosidian/mirror/tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md
